thread.title: Apple, Pot Stocks Show Sickly Losses | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Apple, Pot Stocks Show Sickly Losses | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Wall Street continued to retreat in measured form. Apple ( AAPL ) and cannabis-focused companies performed badly. Yet the action in the stock market today also reflected an ongoing institutional appetite for companies in select retail, medical and consumer-oriented sectors.
X Apple sank further below its critical 200-day moving average with a nearly 2.9% drubbing. Marijuana play Tilray ( TLRY ) got slammed 10% and threatened to cross below 100.
The marijuana-based developer of medicinal products reported a net loss of 20 cents a share in the third quarter. That equals the combined 20 cents a share it lost in the first and second quarters of this year. Revenue in Q3 rose 86% to $10.1 million.
Pot Stocks Fall Hard Tilray, after its parabolic rise in October that ended with an all-time high of 300, is now 66% below that peak. Such a correction is perfectly normal for a stock that rises more than fivefold in such a short time, after a breakout past a 34.20 correct buy point .
The Nasdaq composite, S&P 500 and Dow Jones industrial average all fell 0.6% to 0.7%. Small caps did a smidgen better. The Russell 2000 eased 0.5%.
Utilities got knocked. The Dow Jones utility average fell more than 1.2%. The Philadelphia semiconductor index, or the SOX, gained 0.6%.
Volume was running mildly higher vs. the same time on Tuesday on both main exchanges.
Doing Better Than The Pot Stocks Lately An analysis of IBD's 197 industry groups shows just seven industry groups rallying 1% or more over the past five sessions. They are the following: retail and wholesale auto parts, specialty retail, residential and commercial building, wholesale drug supply, periodicals, drugstore chains, and leisure products retailing.
These groups reflect a robust American consumer. But they also indicate some bargain-hunting by fund managers, given the walloping taken by homebuilders. None of the group's components show a Composite Rating of 90 or higher, according to IBD Stock Checkup. Pulte Group ( PHM ) has the highest Composite score of 57 on a scale of 1 (poor) to 99 (excellent).
The industry group, on a price-weighted basis, has rallied 14% from its late-October low. But it's facing upside resistance at its sharply falling 50-day moving average.
Meanwhile, MarketSmith , IBD's advanced stock chart and screening service, notes at least 19 stocks "near a pivot." This means the stocks are approaching proper buy points.
They include Estee Lauder ( EL ), part of the cosmetics and personal care group, CVS Health ( CVS ) of the drugstores industry group, plus Ollie's Bargain Outlet ( OLLI ), American Express ( AXP ) and Eli Lilly ( LLY ).
Estee Lauder, according to the pattern recognition value-added feature of MarketSmith, has been building a new base that features elements of a double bottom .
In Other Financial Markets Crude oil rebounded some but remains in a bear market. The yield on the benchmark U.S. Treasury 10-year bond dropped to 3.11%, down from 3.14% at the start of November.
